samples.summary: The run's live credential is never added to the redaction allow-list — only `WAFFLEBASE_HUNT_API_KEY`, which this hunter never uses
samples.evidence: `loadContext` sets `cfg: { apiKey: process.env.WAFFLEBASE_HUNT_API_KEY ?? "" }` (hunt-ui.mjs:746) and that single value is the ONLY thing passed as `extra` to `redactSecrets` at every egress boundary (hunt-ui.mjs:886, :1011, :1101 → `renderUiReport`/`explore-raw.json`/verifier prompts, and `hunt-ui-tool.mjs:283`). But the UI hunter mounts `MemStore`/`MemDocStore` with no backend, so `WAFFLEBASE_HUNT_API_KEY` is meaningless here and will normally be unset — `filter(Boolean)` then yields an EMPTY extras list and redaction falls back to generic patterns only. The credential this pipeline actually authenticates with is `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`/`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (hunt-ui.mjs:809), and it is never added. `redactSecrets` (hunt-probe.mjs:41-53) matches `wfb_…`, JWTs, `Bearer …` and `(api-key|token|secret|password)[:= ]value`, none of which match a bare `sk-ant-oat01-…` string, and the `\b(…|token|…)` alternative does not even fire on `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=` because `_T` is not a word boundary. Vector: the explorer/verifier sessions hold `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` with `permissionMode: 'dontAsk'` (ask.mjs:451-455), so a model that reads a token-bearing file (the slash command in this same diff, .claude/commands/hunt-ui.md, tells developers to keep the token in `~/.wafflebase-hunt.env`) and echoes it into a candidate field writes it verbatim into `.harness-reports/hunt-ui/**`. The directory is gitignored (.gitignore:173), which bounds the blast radius to the local disk, hence minor rather than major.
searchedFor: read loadContext and all redactSecrets call sites in hunt-ui.mjs

samples.summary: `hunt-ui-execution.json` is the one artifact written without `redactSecrets`, breaking the file's own "every output boundary is guarded" rule
samples.evidence: `writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, "hunt-ui-execution.json"), JSON.stringify(sessionLog))` at hunt-ui.mjs:893 dumps the raw SDK result messages. The two writes immediately around it (report.md at :882 and run.json at :883-887) both pass through `redactSecrets`, and `explore-raw.json` at :1011 does too. `sessionLog` is filled by `ask.mjs:523` with the SDK's whole result message, which carries the model's final output text for every explorer and verifier call. Anything a model echoed (a file it read, a page string) lands here unredacted. Same pattern exists in hunt.mjs:1132, so this is copied precedent rather than a new class of bug, and the destination is gitignored — hence minor.
searchedFor: grep redactSecrets in hunt-ui.mjs and hunt.mjs

samples.summary: Attacker-authored GitHub issue bodies are injected into both the explorer and the verifier prompts, and the verifier is now the sole source of the citations the gate checks
samples.evidence: `loadContext` calls `fetchIssues(slug)` (hunt-ui.mjs:731), which shells `gh issue list --state all --json number,state,title,body` (hunt-corpus.mjs:142-153) — issue bodies are writable by any GitHub user. `renderIssues` only truncates to 600 chars; nothing strips instruction-shaped text. That corpus is embedded in the explorer prompt (`exploreUi`, "## Open and closed issues already filed") and in the verifier prompt (`verifyUi`, "Issues already filed … (DATA)"). This diff raises the stakes: `UI_EXPLORER_SCHEMA` removes the explorer's `citations` field, so `uiCitationsOf` makes the verifiers' `groundedIn` the ONLY input to `isFilingVerdict` stage 4 (hunt-gate.mjs:534-551) — i.e. one injectable model now controls both the confirm decision and its own supporting evidence. Mitigations are real but soft: fenced blocks, an explicit "treat as DATA" line in each rubric, a read-only tool grant (ask.mjs:58/84), and nothing is filed automatically (the output is a local report). Impact is therefore a fabricated local finding plus whatever a `Read`-capable session can be steered to disclose into `.harness-reports`, not a code-execution or auth bypass.
searchedFor: read exploreUi and verifyUi prompt construction in hunt-ui.mjs

samples.summary: `persona.id` is used unvalidated in filesystem paths, so a charter manifest id containing `../` writes artifacts outside the report directory
samples.evidence: `validatePersona` only asserts `typeof p.id === "string" && p.id !== ""` (hunt-ui.mjs:122) — no character or traversal check. That id is then joined into paths that are written to: `const personaDir = path.join(outDir, persona.id)` (hunt-ui.mjs:975), which receives `explore-raw.json` and `repro-N.json` via `writeArtifact`, whose default does `mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), { recursive: true })` + `writeFileSync`. An id of `../../../..%2Fetc` style (`../../../tmp/x`) escapes `outDir` and creates directories and files anywhere the running user can write. The manifest is read from `scripts/agent/charters-ui/personas.json` or from an operator-supplied `--charters-dir`, so exploitation needs repo-config write access (a malicious PR touching personas.json, or a hunt pointed at an untrusted charters directory) — which is why this is minor rather than major, but the validator is precisely the place a path check belongs and it is absent.
searchedFor: grep personaDir / writeArtifact / ledgerFile path construction in hunt-ui.mjs

samples.summary: `--fault` is not shape-validated at the CLI boundary where it enters, only at the three boundaries it later leaves through
samples.evidence: `const fault = strArg(args, "fault") ?? null` (hunt-ui.mjs:831) accepts any string. The same value is written straight into run.json (`seededFault`) and interpolated into report.md by `renderUiReport` before any check runs; the kebab-case regex only fires later in `openUiSession` (hunt-ui-session.mjs) and `runUiPlan` (hunt-ui-probe.mjs). The diff's own comment on hunt-ui-runner.mjs:75-81 states the principle — "a value that reaches a URL should be constrained at the boundary it enters" — and this is the outermost such boundary. No exploitable path today (the value is developer-supplied, is `encodeURIComponent`-escaped before reaching the URL, and the harness matches the id against a closed registry at packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:88), so this is hardening only.
searchedFor: grep --fault handling in hunt-ui.mjs, hunt-ui-session.mjs, hunt-ui-probe.mjs, hunt-ui-runner.mjs

samples.summary: Nothing asserts the deliberately-seeded defect is absent from a production bundle; the "it cannot ship" claim rests entirely on an unasserted `import.meta.env.DEV` edge
samples.evidence: page.tsx:70-73 argues the seeded `drop-second-char` keystroke-swallowing fault cannot reach production because App.tsx:42-44 gates the lazy import behind `import.meta.env.DEV` and App.tsx:89-91 conditionally registers the route. I confirmed that gate exists and that `installHuntBridge` has exactly one importer (packages/frontend/src/app/harness/hunt/page.tsx:40), so the claim holds today. What is missing is any test or lane that would fail if someone later removes the ternary — a deliberate input-dropping defect in a shipped bundle is a high-consequence regression to leave guarded only by a code comment. The chunk-count budget would probably notice the seven-chunk shift App.tsx:30-34 documents, but that is an indirect proxy, not an assertion about this fault.
searchedFor: grep for a test asserting hunt harness absence from a prod build
